messages:
maria-security: Heads up — we're proposing a shorter retention window for SIEM-exported app logs for customer-facing services. Suggestion: default 90d for exported copies, with 1y archived encrypted snapshots only accessible via JIT unwrap. Thoughts?
john-sre: 90d seems reasonable for signal vs cost. How will we handle investigations that need >90d? do we have a legal/forensics exception flow?
lee-platsec: +1 to 90d default. For exceptions we should require a documented justification ticket and a timeboxed CMK grant. No permanent key grants.
sam-ops: Ops question — how do we implement the JIT unwrap? do we want an ephemeral token service or IAM short-lived creds?
maria-security: thinking ephemeral export tokens minted by export-proxy for up to 72h, backed by KMS envelope key which audit-bot records. The unwrap action requires an approval step in the ticket system.
tess-legal: We need to capture purpose and approver for any >90d access. Also retention exceptions should include custodian and end-date. Legal needs an export log retained for 7 years. Can audit-bot keep that meta?
audit-bot: auto: export-event recorded: id=exp-7160004321-1, actor=maria-security, target_service=payments-api, retention_override=180d, ticket=SEC-8423, timestamp=7160004321
john-sre: Good — ensure that the export payload is redacted for PII by default (email, cc, ssn). If someone requests raw, that must be listed in the ticket and go through ops + legal.
lee-platsec: Proposed RBAC change: add role `siem_exporter:temporary-unmask` scoped to token-lifetime. Workflow: request -> approver (security lead) -> mint token with `unmask` bit -> KMS unwrap allowed. Implementation notes: policy snippet:```json
{
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect":"Allow",
    "Principal":"arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/siem_exporter",
    "Action":["kms:Decrypt"],
    "Condition":{"NumericLessThan":{"kms:TokenIssueTime": "+259200"}}
  }]
}
```
sam-ops: That condition key won't exist raw in most KMS providers; we might need a proxy that checks token attrs before calling KMS. export-proxy approach is fine.
maria-security: Agree. We should also hard-limit export size and strip query params. Example command we want to permit: `./export-proxy --ticket SEC-8423 --service payments-api --ttl 72h`
tess-legal: Also require data subject check for EU tenants — if tenant data included, export must be stored in EU region and retention shorter per local policy. Add region tag to ticket template.
john-sre: Operationally, can we attach a retention TTL to the exported artifact and have storage auto-delete? S3 lifecycle + object tag looks ok. Anyone object to auto-delete? :thinking_face:
lee-platsec: No objections. But implement immutability window for legal holds where an admin can extend via documented hold. Holds must be rare and logged.
audit-bot: auto: policy-change-proposal noted: SIEM default-export-retention=90d, archive-retention=365d, exception-flow=SEC-TICKET, id=policy-5167
maria-security: Next steps: I'll write the exception ticket template and a short PR for export-proxy that enforces token minting + KMS envelope. @john-sre can you scope S3 lifecycle rules? @sam-ops can you prototype proxy behavior?
john-sre: On it, will draft S3 lifecycle and immutability-runbook.
sam-ops: I'll prototype proxy; will include a stubbed approval endpoint for now.
tess-legal: I'll review ticket template for compliance language.
lee-platsec: I'll draft RBAC change doc and a minimal threat model for JIT unwrap. Short follow-up: do we want an alert when someone requests >90d? I want noisy alerting.
maria-security: Yes — make it high-severity to security channel and create a pager when >90d unwrap approved.
lee-platsec: cool. closing for now — will post PR links when ready. :white_check_mark:
